title: County of Berga
capsule: The County of Berga was a small Catalan feudal county in the eastern Pyrenean foothills, originally a dependency of the County of Cerdanya and then of the larger Catalan comital structure. By the eleventh century Berga had its own line of counts descended from Catalan Pyrenean nobility; a viscountship was created alongside the county and eventually sold to the Crown of Aragon under Peter II. The county was absorbed into the County of Barcelona's political orbit and by 1236 had lost its independent status, becoming part of the consolidated Crown of Aragon. Its main town, Berga, served as a highland market center and episcopal suffragen of the bishopric of Urgell throughout the medieval period.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent is only approximately known; the county's highland boundaries were defined by mountain topography rather than formal surveyed limits, and source coverage for this minor county is thin.
